author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: done_a_o is a clk_a flop reset by rst_b_n, the other domain's reset, while its data comes from rst_a_n flops. A producer reset leaves done stale, rst_a_n assertion changes its D asynchronously, and rst_b_n releases it at an arbitrary clk_a phase.

author_reading.rationale: The producer-domain done flag is reset by the destination reset rather than its own, so a producer-domain reset leaves done high until the next start. The flag is software-visible status only.

labels.rationale: done_a_o is a clk_a register that is reset by rst_b_n, the reset of the other clock domain. Its reset release is unsynchronised to clk_a, and its data comes from rst_a_n logic, so the crossing is wrong in both clock and reset.

B reset clears done_a_o without clearing the A-domain finish pipeline or run flag. A finish already in flight can set done after B restarts, and the raw B reset also directly releases the A-clock flop.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical and class. RDC-004 (same-clock source reset by rst_a_n, destination by rst_b_n, as B lists) and RDC-003 for the rst_b_n/clk_a pair (as A lists) both target the wrong-domain reset of done_a_o. RDC-005 does not apply to done_a_o, because its fan-in is clk_a only.
